$comment: THE hand-written part. Four packages -- ui, js, php, py -- are generated from this directory and are never edited. Meta publishes no machine-readable spec for the Graph API, so every fact here is read from its own reference documentation.
title: Facebook Lead Ads

authorize.$comment: Same as facebook-pages: Meta takes the token as a QUERY PARAMETER, and appsecret_proof has to go in the query regardless, so both live in one place and a request stays readable in a log.

proof.$comment: hash_hmac('sha256', $access_token, $app_secret) -- an HMAC over the TOKEN, KEYED BY THE SECRET. The two are one swap apart and both orders produce a plausible 64-character hex string, which is why the parity suite pins a known vector rather than checking the shape.

oauth.$refreshTokenRotates: There is nothing to rotate -- refreshTokenCredential is null. It is stated anyway because a reader who sees only `null` should not have to work out whether the question was skipped or does not apply, and the two look identical from outside.
oauth.$scopeComment: FIVE, and each is load-bearing. leads_retrieval reads a lead's field_data -- without it the lead resolves with the personal data omitted rather than failing, which is the reassuring failure. pages_manage_ads is what Meta requires alongside it for lead access. pages_manage_metadata is what lets the app SUBSCRIBE to the Page's leadgen webhook; without it the trigger never fires and nothing reports why. pages_show_list and pages_read_engagement are the standard Page pair. All are subject to App Review, and leads_retrieval additionally requires the app to pass Meta's Business Verification.
oauth.$comment: The PAGE token, as with facebook-pages. Leads belong to a Page's forms, and Meta requires the token to be held by somebody who can advertise on the ad account. pageAccessToken is `account`-scoped -- one per connected Page -- while appSecret and the client pair are `provider`, one per installation. Getting that backwards is one advertiser reading another's leads, which here means somebody else's customers' names, emails and phone numbers.

$sandboxComment: CHECKED. Meta's Lead Ads Testing Tool submits a TEST lead against a real form on a real Page, and it fires the real webhook -- which is a way to exercise the integration, not a test estate: the lead lands in the same place a real one does and is deleted by hand. There is no separate host, no separate account, and no mode flag on the request. So `none`, and the faker is the way to build against this.
sandboxNote: Facebook Lead Ads has no sandbox. Meta's Lead Ads Testing Tool creates a test lead on the REAL form, which fires the real webhook and appears alongside real leads until somebody deletes it. Anything this reads is real customer data belonging to a real advertiser.
$baseUrlComment: v25.0, not the newest. Meta supports a version for roughly two years -- v25.0 runs to 2028-07-29 -- and versioned changes land on the NEWEST version immediately and reach older ones later. So the newest buys a few months of runway and takes every breaking change first; v25.0 has been out since February and is the one with a long, quiet remainder. An unversioned call silently gets the OLDEST still-supported version, which is why the segment is pinned at all.

credentialFields.label: App ID
credentialFields.help: From the Meta app dashboard. ONE value for the whole installation.

credentialFields.label: App secret (OAuth)
credentialFields.help: The same app's client secret, used to exchange the authorization code.

credentialFields.label: App secret (proof and webhook signature)
credentialFields.help: TWO roles, one value. It keys the appsecret_proof HMAC on outgoing calls, and it is also what Meta signs INCOMING webhook deliveries with -- there is no per-endpoint webhook secret in the Graph API the way there is in Stripe. It is never sent in either direction. For a standard Meta app this is the same value as the OAuth client secret; it is declared separately because they are different roles, and an app that rotates one without the other should not silently break the other.

credentialFields.label: Page access token
credentialFields.help: PER PAGE, not per user. Leads belong to a Page's forms, and Meta requires the token to be held by somebody who can advertise on the ad account. A long-lived page token lasts about 60 days and is re-authorised rather than refreshed.
